Held at CONDITIONAL because the live DOH advisory list could not be read, Thursday's flash-flood runoff is still inside DOH's ~48-hour flushing guidance until about 4 PM today, and long-period south energy (17–20 s in the model) arrives this afternoon. beginner.headline: Today (Sat Oct 10): conditional for beginners. Canoes about 2–3 ft+ (thigh to stomach, Surfline model this morning) with ENE trades about 10 mph gusting near 18 mph, grooming but pushing seaward. Exposed south shores 5–7 ft AM easing to 4–6 ft PM (NWS), Canoes far smaller. Water color decides: still inside the ~48-hour flush after Thursday's flash flooding.
beginner.recommendation: Plan for 10:30 AM–1:30 PM: tide rising off the 10:07 AM low (0.4 ft), the lightest wind of the day in model runs (about 8–9 mph E), and ahead of the 17–20 s forerunners the model shows from about 2 PM. Go only if the water at Canoes and toward the Kūhiō drains / Ala Wai side is visibly clear and several full set cycles look manageable. One student or a small group of strong adults; several students or children only with clear water and low drift. Trades are cross-offshore at Waikīkī, so expect seaward drift of students and boards, stronger in gusts.

water.why: The live DOH Clean Water Branch advisory list (eha-cloud.doh.hawaii.gov/cwb) could not be loaded this run. The DOH CWB home page lists no advisories itself (it links to the live list). safetoswimhawaii.com showed no loaded advisory data and is not official. water.runoff: Brown, gray, cloudy or turbid water, or visible runoff: don't go in, advisory or not. DOH guidance: storm-runoff water can carry sewage and pathogens; coastal water usually needs about 48 hours to flush.
